🇲🇽🗳️ <u>Sheinbaum: Claim That Washington Picked Morena's Candidates Is "Absurd"</u>

PT national leader Alberto Anaya claimed US pressure shaped Morena's choice of state coordinators for 2027, when 17 governorships and the entire Chamber of Deputies are on the ballot. Sheinbaum's answer at Thursday's mañanera: "It's absurd, really, what he's saying has no basis at all." Morena has picked its coordinators by poll since its founding, she said, and sometimes the person a party wanted doesn't come out on top, "and they make these interpretations that have no basis."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Crucifix, Skull and Dagger: The Secret Anti-Communist Lodge Inside UNAM</u>

Mexican intelligence files from the DFS and DGIPS held in the Archivo General de la Nación, plus a declassified CIA document, reconstruct for the first time how the MURO worked inside UNAM in the 1960s: recruits from elite Catholic schools, a secret oath sworn before a crucifix, a skull and a dagger, shock brigades that broke up leftist meetings with tear gas, and members planted at the head of student societies without revealing who they answered to. Business sectors close to alemanismo helped fund its propaganda. The CIA's own file from August 5, 1965 described the group as "fascist and antisemitic."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>800 Miners Strike at Canadian-Owned First Majestic Mine in Durango</u>

At noon on October 8, Sections 21 and 22 of Mexico's National Mining Union raised red-and-black strike flags over the Tayoltita underground gold and silver mine in San Dimas, Durango. The charges against Canada's First Majestic: violations of the collective contract and of union freedom, deteriorated machinery kept running on provisional repairs, accidents that have cost workers' lives, and a profit-based bonus for 2025 that was owed in 2026 and never paid.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum Hosts 30+ US and Mexican Business Leaders at the National Palace</u>

US Ambassador Ronald Johnson and the American Chamber of Commerce sat down with President Sheinbaum for an hour and a half on Thursday. On the table: confidence in Mexico as a destination for US investment and closing out the T-MEC review. CCE president José Medina Mora called it a high-level meeting and said the American executives left very happy that the President listened to their plans to expand. The numbers behind the mood: foreign direct investment hit $35 billion in the first half of 2026, 14% above 2024, and this year's growth forecast has been revised from 0.8% to 1.5%.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Three of Five Banxico Board Members Open the Door to Another Rate Cut</u>

The minutes of Banxico's September 24 decision, which unanimously held the rate at 6.50%, show three board members ready to weigh a further cut, citing slack in the economy and ongoing disinflation, El Economista reports. Governor Victoria Rodríguez wrote that "in following decisions a specific reduction in the reference rate could be evaluated." One member pointed to the "atonía," or sluggishness, of economic activity and an "absence of demand pressures on prices." Only one member raised the need to move in step with the Federal Reserve.

🇲🇽🏘️ <u>8 in 10 Mexicans Cut Food or Health Spending to Keep a Roof Overhead</u>

Habitat for Humanity's report "A home, but at what cost?", based on 30,758 surveys in 22 countries, found that 8 out of 10 people in Mexico spent less on food or medical care in the past year to cover their housing costs. 56% say a single unexpected expense could cost them their home, eight points above the global average of 48%. 37% live with damp, mold or other unhealthy conditions, compared with 23% globally. And 57.3% of Mexico's homes were built by the families themselves, often without technical help or formal financing.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Top Auditor Wants Audits With Teeth</u>

Federal Superior Auditor Aureliano Hernández Palacios Cardel asked lawmakers to reform the legal framework and "give teeth to the oversight bodies," so that audits end in sanctions that actually deter corruption. Launching the ASF's audits of 2025 federal spending in Mexico City's boroughs, he called for accountability that is "much more effective, much faster, much more proactive." Javier Herrera Borunda, who chairs the Chamber of Deputies' ASF oversight committee, backed him and said more reforms could come before year-end, adding to those in force since May 2026 that move auditing from reactive to proactive with big data and agreements with the SAT, the UIF and the CNBV.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexican Forces Arrest "El Tanque," the CJNG Fuel-Theft Boss Washington Only Sanctioned</u>

Iván Cazarín Molina, alias El Tanque, was arrested in Zapopan, Jalisco, on October 5 in a joint operation by the Defense Ministry, the Navy, the National Guard and the SSPC. Mexican authorities identify him as a regional CJNG leader and one of El Mencho's trusted operators. The US Treasury put him on its OFAC list back in September 2024 for running a network that siphoned fuel from Pemex pipelines and sold it through front companies, part of it bound for the US market, generating tens of millions of dollars a year.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico to the OAS Council's New Chair: Stay Neutral</u>

Ecuador's Mónica Palencia took over the OAS Permanent Council on October 1. She was a minister in Daniel Noboa's government when Ecuadorian police stormed Mexico's embassy in Quito in April 2024. At her first session, Mexico's representative Alejandro Encinas asked her to stay neutral, "especially in this multilateral body, where there is great diversity of ideas and thoughts, far removed from the fundamentalism of single thinking." Palencia's reply: "Rest assured that I am not a supporter of single thinking."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Hits an All-Time Record: 22.9 Million Formal Jobs</u>

Mexico closed September with 22,927,276 jobs registered with the IMSS, the highest figure since the indicator has existed. 128,803 formal jobs were created in September alone, bringing the 2026 total to 410,200. Permanent positions also hit a record at 19,967,281, or 87.1% of the total. Extractive industries (+5.2%) and transport and communications (+4.8%) led annual growth.
